facts.fact: BCT Note n°2026-132 of 5 May 2026 is addressed to banks, the Post and payment institutions (établissements de paiement) and names payment institutions, alongside banks and the Post, as issuers of mobile wallets in Tunisia; it names no law or rules.

systems.owner: Banque Centrale de Tunisie (label); Société Monétique Tunisie manages the mobile payment system

facts.fact: La Presse reports that the BCT licensing commission granted OFT Tunisie, a subsidiary of Ooredoo FinTech International, definitive authorisation as a resident payment institution, published in JORT n°29 in the week before 16 March 2026 after approval in principle in December 2024, and that 16 payment service providers are licensed in Tunisia; the article names no law.

Challenges reports that BCT circulaire n°2026-10 imposes a mandatory annual cyber audit and stronger governance on payment institutions, keeps ceilings on accounts and transfers, and enters into force three months after its issue (published 2026-09-25 per the article's date context; the article gives no day).
facts.system: BCT circulaire n°2026-10 on payment institutions

facts.fact: Challenges reports that BCT circulaire n°2026-10 of September 2026 regulates payment institutions (établissements de paiement), which are not banks, setting audit and governance duties and ceilings on their accounts and transfers.
facts.system: BCT circulaire n°2026-10 on payment institutions

note: Reports a BCT note on the TUNPAY visual label for banks, payment institutions and the post; it names no payments law or rule on licensing or connection, so no fact.

facts.fact: The Central Bank of Tunisia issued Circular n° 2026-10 on payment establishments on 25 September 2026, binding rules on their services, accounts, agents and governance; it takes effect three months after publication.
facts.system: Circulaire BCT n° 2026-10 relative aux établissements de paiement

facts.fact: Article 51 repeals and replaces Circular n° 2018-16 of 31 December 2018 on the activity and functioning of payment establishments, which was therefore in force until then.
facts.system: Circulaire BCT n° 2018-16 relative aux établissements de paiement

facts.fact: Article 39 refers to Circular n° 2020-11 of 18 May 2020 on the conditions for providing domestic mobile payment services as a text that applies alongside it.
facts.system: Circulaire BCT n° 2020-11 relative aux services de paiement mobile domestique

facts.fact: Circular 2026-10 authorises payment establishments to open three tiers of client payment accounts, transfer funds and issue electronic payment instruments, and requires the BCT to keep a register and publish a list of licensed establishments (Articles 1, 16, 42).
facts.system: Circulaire BCT n° 2026-10 relative aux établissements de paiement

facts.fact: Article 3 of Circular 2026-10 requires payment establishments to join the payment and clearing systems suited to their activities; the circular takes effect three months after 25 September 2026.
facts.system: Circulaire BCT n° 2026-10 relative aux établissements de paiement

facts.fact: BCT Circular n° 2024-5 of 13 February 2024 sets the binding rules for the activity of managing payment systems and securities settlement systems, including governance and risk minimums.
facts.system: Circulaire BCT n° 2024-5 sur la gestion des systèmes de paiement

facts.fact: Law n° 2016-48 of 11 July 2016 on banks and financial institutions was adopted by parliament on 9 June 2016 and promulgated, and its Articles 20 and 21 set the framework for payment services and payment establishments.
facts.system: Loi n° 2016-48 relative aux banques et aux établissements financiers

facts.fact: Article 20 of Law 2016-48 has payment services run by a resident financial institution as a specialised payment establishment, which is not a bank, with minimum capital of 5 million dinars under Article 32.
facts.system: Loi n° 2016-48 relative aux banques et aux établissements financiers
